records.title: Hybrid Battery Pack Degradation
records.description: The CT200h NiMH hybrid battery pack loses capacity over time, reducing fuel economy and hybrid system effectiveness. The CT200h uses the same hybrid system as the Toyota Prius, and battery degradation follows a similar pattern. Hot climates accelerate degradation, and cells can develop internal resistance imbalances.
records.solution: Replace the hybrid battery pack with a new or refurbished unit. The CT200h battery is the same as the third-generation Prius, so aftermarket options are plentiful and affordable. Refurbished packs from Green Bean Battery or hybrid specialists cost $1,200-$2,000 installed.
symptoms: Engine runs more frequently than expected

records.title: Electric Water Pump Premature Failure
records.description: The electric water pump on the CT200h hybrid system fails prematurely, causing coolant circulation loss for the hybrid inverter and electric motor. Unlike conventional belt-driven water pumps, this is an electric unit that controls coolant flow to the high-voltage hybrid components. Failure can lead to hybrid system overheating and shutdown.
records.solution: Replace the electric water pump assembly. Use the OEM Toyota/Lexus part for the hybrid cooling circuit. After replacement, bleed the hybrid cooling system thoroughly to remove air pockets. Check the coolant level in both the engine and hybrid cooling circuits.
symptoms: Coolant leak from electric pump area
Hybrid system shuts down in hot weather

citations.title: ClubLexus.com — CT200h electric water pump failure diagnosis and replacement

communityRecommendations.content: The CT200h has TWO separate cooling systems — one for the engine and one for the hybrid components. Make sure both are maintained with fresh coolant at the recommended intervals.

records.title: Brake Actuator Buzzing and Grinding Noise
records.description: The electronic brake actuator on the 2019+ ES produces a noticeable buzzing or grinding noise during low-speed braking and when the brake hold function is engaged. The noise comes from the ABS actuator cycling at low speeds and is a design characteristic of the brake-by-wire system. While not a safety concern, the noise is prominent enough to be heard in the cabin.
records.solution: Lexus released a software update (TSB) to modify the brake actuator operation and reduce noise. Visit the dealer for the ECU reflash. Some noise may persist at very low speeds as this is inherent to the brake-by-wire design. Adding sound deadening material around the actuator can further reduce cabin intrusion.
symptoms: Buzzing or grinding noise when braking at low speed
Vibration felt through brake pedal during light braking
Noise when brake hold function activates
Groaning sound from engine bay area when releasing brakes

citations.title: Lexus TSB L-SB-0025-20 — brake actuator noise reduction software update for ES/UX/NX

communityRecommendations.content: The TSB software update significantly reduces the noise but may not eliminate it completely. This is a known characteristic of Toyota/Lexus brake-by-wire systems across their TNGA platform.

records.title: Dashboard Melting and Sticky Surface
records.description: Lexus programs ZLD and ZLZ document cracked and/or sticky dashboard surfaces caused over time by heat, humidity and, in ZLZ, light intensity on covered ES 350 vehicles. ZLD covers certain 2007-2008 vehicles and ZLZ covers certain 2008-2012 vehicles, preserving the page’s 2007-2012 identity. The primary records describe a cosmetic condition; they do not support the page’s “dangerous glare” or “2,000+ complaints” claims.
records.solution: Have a Lexus dealer verify the VIN and inspect the dashboard condition. The published ZLD and ZLZ coverage periods were time-limited, so this page does not promise a free repair in 2026; ask Lexus whether any current assistance applies before authorizing dashboard replacement. Avoid solvent or coating experiments that could worsen the surface. No universal retail part or dealer-only remedy is asserted.

citations.title: Warranty Enhancement Program ZLD — 2007-2008 ES 350 dashboard
Customer Support Program ZLZ — 2008-2012 ES 350 dashboard

records.contentUpdateSummary: Corrected the program names to ZLD/ZLZ, bounded coverage to VIN verification and historical terms, and removed the unsupported safety-glare and complaint-count claims.

records.title: Excessive Oil Consumption 2GR-FE Engine
records.description: The 3.5L 2GR-FE V6 in the ES350 consumes excessive oil between changes, often burning 1 quart every 1,500-2,500 miles. The root cause is typically worn piston rings that allow oil past the ring lands into the combustion chamber. Toyota/Lexus issued a TSB acknowledging the issue and revised the piston ring design in later production runs.
records.solution: Perform an oil consumption test at the dealer to document the rate. If consuming more than 1 quart per 1,200 miles, the repair involves replacing piston rings and possibly pistons. Use 0W-20 synthetic oil and check levels every 1,000 miles. Some owners switch to 5W-30 for reduced consumption.
symptoms: Oil level drops significantly between oil changes
Blue smoke from exhaust on startup
Need to add oil every 1,000-2,000 miles

citations.title: Toyota TSB 0094-14 — 2GR-FE oil consumption inspection and piston ring replacement procedure

communityRecommendations.content: Keep meticulous oil top-off records with dated receipts — this documentation is essential for warranty claims and proves the consumption rate to the dealer.

records.title: 1MZ-FE V6 Engine Oil Sludge Failure
records.description: Lexus manufacturer communications filed with NHTSA document a special policy/customer-satisfaction program for oil gelling or sludge on certain 1997-2002 ES300 vehicles with the 1MZ-FE six-cylinder engine. The page's 1997-1999 model years fall within that documented population. The available primary records support the condition and historical repair program, but they do not establish this page's asserted drainback-passage design flaw, cylinder-head heat theory, class-action history, universal bearing damage or short-trip causal rule.
records.solution: If oil gelling or sludge is suspected, stop driving when an oil-pressure warning, abnormal engine noise or loss of oil pressure is present and have the engine inspected under current VIN-specific Lexus service information. The Lexus special policy was historical, so this page does not promise a free repair in 2026. Do not use chemical flushes, repeated 1,000-2,000-mile flushing intervals, a viscosity change or a universal teardown instruction from this page. Follow the owner-manual oil specification and maintenance schedule unless current Lexus service information directs otherwise. No universal retail part or dealer-only remedy is asserted.

Aftermarket refurbished packs from companies like Green Bean Battery or Dorman cost $1,500-$2,500 installed. Individual cell replacement is also possible for partial degradation.

Unable to enter or maintain EV mode

records.title: Dashboard Melting and Sticky Surface
records.description: The GS dashboard suffers from the same melting and sticky surface defect as other Lexus models of this era. Heat exposure causes the dashboard material to chemically degrade, resulting in a shiny, tacky surface that creates dangerous glare on the windshield. This was a widespread issue across the Lexus lineup.
records.solution: Lexus Customer Support Program ZE7 covers dashboard replacement. Contact your dealer or Lexus customer support at 1-800-255-3987. The entire dashboard assembly and associated trim panels are replaced with redesigned materials.

Reflective glare on windshield from melted dashboard
Chemical smell from dashboard in warm weather

citations.title: NHTSA complaint cluster — Lexus GS dashboard melting defect (500+ complaints)

records.title: Power Steering Rack Seal Leak
records.description: The power steering rack develops internal seal leaks that cause power steering fluid loss. The leak typically appears at the inner tie rod boots where fluid seeps past the rack seals. Low fluid levels lead to increased steering effort and pump whining noise, and eventually the rack must be replaced.
records.solution: Replace the power steering rack assembly. Remanufactured racks are available from Maval and Cardone at significant savings over new OEM. Perform a complete power steering fluid flush after installation. Inspect tie rods and replace if worn.
symptoms: Power steering fluid leaking from rack area
Whining noise when turning steering wheel
Increased steering effort especially at low speed

citations.title: ClubLexus.com — GS steering rack leak diagnosis and replacement options

communityRecommendations.content: Check the inner tie rod boots regularly for fluid wetness — this is the earliest sign of a leaking rack. Catching it early prevents pump damage from running low on fluid.

records.title: Water Pump Premature Failure
records.description: The water pump on the GS models fails prematurely, typically between 60,000-100,000 miles. Coolant leaks from the weep hole as the internal seal deteriorates, and the pump bearing develops play causing a whining noise. If not addressed, overheating and potential engine damage can occur.
records.solution: Replace the water pump assembly and thermostat together as a preventive measure. Use OEM or high-quality aftermarket parts (Aisin brand is the OEM supplier). Replace the serpentine belt and tensioner at the same time if they show wear.
symptoms: Coolant leak from front of engine
Whining noise from water pump area at idle
Sweet coolant smell from engine bay

citations.title: ClubLexus.com — GS350 water pump failure pattern and replacement guide

communityRecommendations.content: Aisin WPT-190 water pump — this is the actual OEM supplier for Toyota/Lexus water pumps at a fraction of the dealer price. Identical quality.

records.title: 2JZ-GE Timing Belt Service - Interval Confusion and Interference Engine Risk
records.description: The 2JZ-GE inline-six in the 1993-1997 GS300 (JZS147) uses a rubber timing belt with Lexus's factory replacement interval set at 90,000 miles, while the same engine in the Toyota Supra is specified at 110,000 miles - causing widespread owner confusion about the correct service interval. Although the 2JZ-GE is often described as 'non-interference,' multiple sources and shop reports document bent valves when the belt fails, jumps a tooth, or is installed with incorrect timing. Service requires removing the radiator, fan shroud, crank pulley, and timing covers, and most independents replace the water pump, idler/tensioner pulleys, cam/crank seals, and accessory belts at the same time. Aged hydraulic tensioners and oil-soaked belts from leaking front cam seals are commonly found during the job.
records.solution: Replace the timing belt at 90,000 miles per Lexus factory schedule (do not stretch to Supra's 110k interval on a Lexus chassis). Replace the hydraulic tensioner, idler pulley, water pump, thermostat, drive belts, and front cam/crank seals at the same time - labor to access these parts is the bulk of the job. Use OEM Aisin or Toyota/Mitsuboshi belt. Verify cam and crank timing marks at TDC #1 before reinstalling covers, and rotate the engine two full revolutions by hand to confirm no valve-to-piston contact before cranking with the starter.
symptoms: Squealing or chirping from front of engine
Visible cracks, glazing, or missing teeth on timing belt
Engine cranks but will not start after belt jumps or breaks
Oil contamination of timing belt from front cam/crank seal leak
Rough running or no compression after belt failure (bent valves)

citations.title: Engine Maintenance: Timing Belt Replacement on Lexus GS 300s - Underhood Service
Engine Maintenance: Timing Belt Replacement on Lexus GS 300s - Brake & Front End
Timing Belt @ 120K? - 93-05 Lexus GS300/GS400/GS430 - Lexus Owners Club

records.title: Front Lower Control Arm Bushing Failure
records.description: The 1993-1997 GS300 (JZS147) front suspension uses double-wishbone geometry with soft factory rubber bushings in the lower control arms. These bushings crack, separate from the inner sleeve, and rot out as they age, allowing the control arm to walk under braking and acceleration. The result is a hollow 'clunk' or banging from the front end over bumps, wandering steering, uneven inner-edge tire wear, and an inability to hold an alignment. Lexus does not sell the bushing separately at the dealer - the OEM service is to replace the entire control arm assembly, which is expensive. Aftermarket press-in bushing kits (rubber or polyurethane from SuperPro, Whiteline, Prothane) are the cost-effective fix for this generation.
records.solution: Inspect the lower control arm bushings with a pry bar - any visible cracking, separation between the rubber and inner sleeve, or excessive deflection means replace. Remove the lower control arm (disconnect ball joint, sway-bar end link, and the two pivot bolts). Press out the worn bushings and press in OEM-rubber or polyurethane replacements (SuperPro SPF3163K is sized specifically for the 1993-1997 GS300). Reinstall, torque pivot bolts to spec with the suspension loaded at ride height (to avoid pre-loading the new bushings), and perform a four-wheel alignment.
symptoms: Clunking or banging from front end over bumps
Cannot hold a front alignment after adjustment

records.title: AHC (Adaptive Hydraulic) Suspension Leak
records.description: The Kinetic Dynamic Suspension System (KDSS) on the GX460 develops hydraulic fluid leaks from the stabilizer bar actuators and hydraulic lines. Leaks cause the KDSS warning light to illuminate and the system to become inoperative, resulting in increased body roll and a less controlled ride. The front actuators are the most common failure point.
records.solution: Replace the leaking KDSS actuator(s) and hydraulic lines. Refill and bleed the system with the correct Toyota KDSS fluid. Both front and rear actuators should be inspected even if only one is leaking. Some owners disconnect the KDSS system and install conventional sway bars.
symptoms: Clunking noise from suspension over bumps
Visible fluid on stabilizer bar actuators

citations.title: ClubLexus.com — GX460 KDSS leak diagnosis and replacement procedure

communityRecommendations.content: Check KDSS actuators during every oil change by looking for fluid residue on the front and rear stabilizer bars. Catching a leak early prevents damage to the hydraulic pump.

records.title: Center Differential Lock Actuator Failure
records.description: The center differential lock actuator on the GX470 fails due to internal motor wear and electrical contact corrosion. When the actuator fails, the center diff lock cannot be engaged for low-range off-road use. The actuator is mounted on the transfer case and is exposed to road debris and moisture.
records.solution: Replace the center differential lock actuator motor. The actuator is accessible from under the vehicle on the transfer case. Use the OEM Toyota actuator for reliability. After replacement, verify engagement by testing in a straight line at low speed on a loose surface.
symptoms: Center diff lock indicator flashes but does not engage
Center diff lock switch has no effect
Clicking sound from transfer case when trying to engage

citations.title: ClubLexus.com — GX470 center diff lock actuator troubleshooting and replacement

communityRecommendations.content: Exercise the center diff lock monthly by engaging and disengaging it for 30 seconds. This prevents internal corrosion from seizing the actuator motor contacts.

records.title: Secondary Air Injection Pump Failure
records.description: The secondary air injection (SAI) system pump and switching valves fail due to moisture intrusion and corrosion. The SAI pump introduces fresh air into the exhaust during cold starts to reduce emissions, but the pump motor corrodes internally and the switching valves stick. This triggers a check engine light with SAI-related codes.
records.solution: Replace the secondary air injection pump and switching valves. Clean or replace the air injection check valves. Clear codes and verify operation. Some owners in non-emissions-testing states choose to bypass the system entirely with a tune.
symptoms: Check engine light with P2440/P2441/P2442 codes
Whirring noise from passenger side of engine on cold start

citations.title: ClubLexus.com — GX470 secondary air injection system failure guide with part numbers

communityRecommendations.content: Replace both the pump AND the switching valves at the same time — if one has failed, the other is likely close behind. The valves are $150 each but save a second repair.

records.title: Alternator Failure from Age and Oil Contamination Leading to Charging Loss
records.description: First-generation IS300s commonly experience alternator failure as mileage climbs, sometimes accelerated by nearby oil leaks contaminating the unit. Owners report battery warning lights, dimming lights, low system voltage, and stalling after the battery discharges. Because the car may continue running briefly on battery power, the problem is sometimes mistaken for a bad battery alone.
records.solution: Test charging voltage at idle and under load, and inspect for oil leakage from the valve cover or power steering area that may have reached the alternator. Replace the alternator with a quality OEM or Denso unit and correct any fluid leaks that contributed to failure. The battery should be load-tested afterward because repeated deep discharge can damage it.

communityRecommendations.content: Owners frequently recommend Denso/OEM alternators over low-cost reman units because cheaper replacements often have short service life.
Fix valve cover leaks before installing a new alternator so the replacement is not contaminated.

records.title: Carbon Buildup on Intake Valves (2.0T)
records.description: The direct-injected 2.0L turbo four-cylinder in the IS200t/IS300 accumulates heavy carbon deposits on the intake valves since fuel is not sprayed over the valves to clean them. This leads to rough idle, hesitation under acceleration, and reduced power output typically between 40,000-80,000 miles.
records.solution: Perform a walnut shell blasting of the intake valves to remove carbon deposits. This requires removing the intake manifold and using specialized media blasting equipment. Plan to repeat every 40,000-60,000 miles. Using a quality catch can helps slow the buildup rate.
symptoms: Reduced power and sluggish throttle response
Slight misfire feel at low RPM

citations.title: ClubLexus.com — IS200t/IS300 carbon buildup walnut blasting guide and interval recommendations

communityRecommendations.content: JLT Performance oil catch can — catches oil vapor before it reaches the intake valves, significantly reducing carbon buildup between walnut blasting services.

claims.content: JLT Performance oil catch can — catches oil vapor before it reaches the intake valves, significantly reducing carbon buildup between walnut blasting services.

records.title: Dashboard Melting and Sticky Surface
records.description: The IS dashboard develops a sticky, melting surface identical to the ES and GS models of the same era. The dashboard material breaks down chemically in heat and sun exposure, creating a reflective glare on the windshield and a tacky feel. Lexus extended warranty coverage through Customer Support Program ZE7.
records.solution: Obtain dashboard replacement under the Lexus Customer Support Program ZE7 extended warranty. If coverage has expired, request goodwill assistance from Lexus corporate. Aftermarket dash covers provide a temporary cosmetic fix but do not resolve the underlying material breakdown.
symptoms: Dashboard surface becomes sticky and tacky
Chemical odor from dashboard in heat

citations.title: NHTSA complaint cluster — Lexus IS dashboard melting defect affecting 2006-2013 models

communityRecommendations.content: Even if you are past the official warranty extension, Lexus customer support has authorized free dashboard replacements on a case-by-case basis. Call 1-800-255-3987 and be persistent.

records.title: Front Door Trim / Inner Garnish Rattle at Speaker Area
records.description: Multiple owners of current-generation Lexus IS models report a persistent rattle or buzzing from the front door panel area, often near the speaker grille or inner garnish, especially on rough pavement or with bass-heavy audio. Lexus issued service guidance for door trim noise on this generation, indicating the condition is known at the dealer level. Owners typically describe the noise as intermittent at first, then easier to reproduce as clips, felt interfaces, or trim contact points loosen slightly.
records.solution: Technicians usually road-test the vehicle to isolate the exact door and trim contact point, then remove the affected door panel and apply anti-rattle felt, foam tape, or updated insulators at the speaker grille, garnish, or clip interfaces. Broken or loose retaining clips should be replaced, and the panel should be reinstalled with proper torque and alignment. If the noise is audio-induced, verify the speaker fasteners and harness routing before reassembly.
symptoms: Buzzing or rattling from front door panel
Noise over bumps or rough roads
Intermittent trim noise near speaker grille

communityRecommendations.content: Before dealer visit, reproduce the noise with bass-heavy audio and note which door and road surface triggers it most consistently.
If DIY-inspecting, check door panel clips and speaker fasteners first; loose clips are a common source of intermittent buzzes.

records.title: Fuel Pump Impeller Failure (Recall)
records.description: The low-pressure fuel pump impeller can deform due to excessive fuel absorption, causing the fuel pump to become inoperative. This results in engine stalling while driving or inability to start, creating a serious safety hazard. Toyota/Lexus issued a massive recall (20V-863) affecting over 1.8 million vehicles across multiple models.
records.solution: Replace the fuel pump assembly at any Lexus dealer free of charge under recall 20V-863. The dealer replaces the entire fuel pump with an updated unit that uses a redesigned impeller. If you have not received a recall notice, contact your dealer with your VIN to verify eligibility.
symptoms: Engine stalls while driving without warning
Engine runs rough or sputters at speed

ClassAction.org: Jan. 2020 Toyota, Lexus Denso Fuel Pump Recall Left Out 2018-2019 Vehicles
ToyotaNation: Toyotas fuel pump recall list thus far

communityRecommendations.content: This is a safety recall — do not delay getting the fuel pump replaced. Engine stalling at highway speed has caused multiple accidents. Check NHTSA.gov with your VIN for recall status.

records.title: LCD Climate Control and Radio Display Pixel Failure
records.description: The factory climate/audio display in the first-gen IS is known for dimming, losing pixels, or becoming unreadable with age. Owners report missing segments, blank screens, and difficulty adjusting HVAC settings at night or in bright daylight. This is a very common age-related electronics issue on 2001-2005 cars.
records.solution: Verify the issue is in the display unit rather than a fuse or backlighting power supply. Repair options include sending the unit to a specialist for LCD/pixel repair, replacing the display assembly with a known-good unit, or converting to an aftermarket audio/HVAC solution where applicable. Used units can fail the same way, so rebuilt parts are often preferred.

citations.title: My.IS and ClubLexus threads documenting IS300 climate/radio display pixel failures

communityRecommendations.content: Owners often prefer specialist rebuild services over salvage-yard replacements because rebuilt units typically address the underlying display failure.
Take photos of connector positions before removing the center stack to avoid reassembly mistakes.

records.title: Lexus Safety System+ False Forward Collision / PCS Warnings from Dirty or Misaligned Sensors
records.description: Some owners report intermittent pre-collision system, radar cruise, or lane-support warnings on 2023-2025 Lexus IS models, often after heavy rain, road grime buildup, windshield contamination, or minor front-end impacts. The system may temporarily disable with a message indicating the camera or radar is unavailable, even though no permanent hardware failure exists. In other cases, sensor alignment or calibration drift after windshield or bumper work can trigger recurring warnings.
records.solution: Inspect and clean the front radar emblem area and windshield camera zone first, then scan for stored ADAS-related codes. If warnings persist, perform radar/camera aiming and calibration, especially after windshield replacement, bumper repair, or alignment work. Replace the affected sensor only after confirming power, communication, and calibration status.
symptoms: ADAS warnings in rain or after car wash

communityRecommendations.content: Clean the radar emblem and the windshield area in front of the camera before assuming a failed sensor.
After windshield replacement, insist on proper camera calibration; many intermittent warnings trace back to skipped ADAS setup.

records.title: Lower Ball Joint Wear or Separation Risk in Front Suspension
records.description: The first-generation IS shares a known Toyota/Lexus weakness involving front lower ball joints that can develop excessive play with age and mileage. Owners report clunking, wandering steering, uneven tire wear, and in severe cases joint separation that can cause loss of control. This is a heavily documented maintenance and safety concern in the IS300 community.
records.solution: Inspect front lower ball joints for play during any suspension or brake service, especially on higher-mileage cars or vehicles with unknown history. Replace worn joints promptly with OEM-quality parts and inspect adjacent components such as tie rods, control arm bushings, and front tires for secondary damage. An alignment should follow replacement.
symptoms: sudden wheel angle change if joint fails

communityRecommendations.content: Owners strongly recommend genuine Toyota/Lexus lower ball joints rather than cheap aftermarket units because failure consequences are severe.
If buying a used IS300, inspect lower ball joints immediately and budget for replacement if service history is unknown.

records.title: Premature Front Brake Squeal / Groan at Low Speed
records.description: A number of owners report front brake squeal, chirp, or groaning noises during light stops, especially when cold, damp, or after the vehicle sits overnight. This is commonly tied to pad material characteristics, rotor surface condition, or insufficient lubrication at pad contact points rather than outright brake failure. The complaint is more of a refinement issue, but it is frequent enough on owner forums and dealer visits to be considered a known nuisance.
records.solution: Inspect pad thickness, rotor finish, and hardware condition first. Dealers or independent shops typically clean and lubricate pad ears/shims, resurface or replace rotors if glazing is present, and install revised pads or shims if available. If the vehicle has F SPORT brakes, verify correct pad compound and bedding procedure after service.
symptoms: Groan when stopping at parking lot speeds
Noise worse when brakes are cold or damp
Brake noise without noticeable loss of stopping power

communityRecommendations.content: Ask for pad/rotor inspection before replacing parts; many cases improve with proper shim lubrication and pad bedding.
If replacing pads, use OEM or a known low-noise ceramic compound to preserve Lexus-level refinement.

records.title: 8-Speed Automatic Harsh Shifting
records.description: The Aisin 8-speed automatic transmission in the third-generation IS exhibits harsh or jerky shifts, particularly during low-speed 1-2 and 2-3 upshifts and when downshifting for deceleration. The transmission control module programming prioritizes fuel economy over smoothness, leading to abrupt gear changes that are felt prominently in the cabin.
records.solution: Visit the dealer for a transmission ECU reprogramming that smooths shift points and torque converter lockup behavior. Perform a transmission fluid drain-and-fill with Toyota WS fluid every 40,000 miles. If harsh shifting persists after the reflash, the valve body may need replacement.
symptoms: Hard jerk during 1-2 upshift at low speed
Transmission hesitation when accelerating from a stop

citations.title: Lexus TSB L-SB-0087-18 — IS transmission shift quality improvement reprogramming

communityRecommendations.content: A fluid drain-and-fill with genuine Toyota WS ATF makes a noticeable difference in shift quality. Do not flush — just drain and refill 4-5 quarts.

records.title: Valve Cover Gasket Leaks Causing Oil Smell and Misfire Risk
records.description: Aging valve cover gaskets on the 2JZ-GE commonly harden and leak, allowing oil to seep onto the cylinder head, spark plug tube seals, and exhaust side of the engine. Owners often notice a burnt-oil smell, visible oil around the valve covers, and occasional misfires if oil contaminates ignition components. This is one of the most common age-related engine leaks on the first-gen IS300.
records.solution: Confirm the leak source by cleaning the engine and inspecting around the valve cover perimeter and spark plug wells. Replace both valve cover gaskets, spark plug tube seals, and related grommets; many owners also replace the PCV valve at the same time to reduce crankcase pressure. If misfires are present, inspect and replace oil-soaked coil boots or plugs.

citations.title: My.IS and ClubLexus threads on IS300 valve cover gasket oil leaks

communityRecommendations.content: Use OEM valve cover gasket sets and replace spark plug tube seals and grommets at the same time to avoid repeat labor.
A PCV valve replacement is cheap preventive maintenance when doing this job.

records.title: Infotainment System Lag and Touchpad Issues
records.description: The LC flagship coupe shares the same frustrating Remote Touch Interface touchpad and laggy infotainment as other Lexus models. On a $100,000+ vehicle, the slow response times and imprecise touchpad control are a particularly sharp contrast to the otherwise exceptional driving experience. The system is widely criticized in professional reviews.
records.solution: Update to the latest infotainment software version. The 2022+ LC received a touchscreen update that significantly improves usability. For pre-2022 models, use Apple CarPlay (added 2020) or voice commands to minimize touchpad interaction.
symptoms: Cursor overshoots targets requiring multiple corrections

citations.title: LexusEnthusiast.com — LC500 infotainment criticism and improvement timeline

communityRecommendations.content: The 2022 infotainment update with touchscreen capability is available as a retrofit for 2018-2021 LC models at the dealer. It is a significant improvement worth the investment.

records.title: Air Suspension Strut and Compressor Failure
records.description: The pneumatic air suspension system on the LS460 and LS600h develops leaks in the air springs, causing the vehicle to sag overnight or drop on one corner. The air compressor runs excessively to compensate for leaks and eventually burns out. Complete air suspension failure leaves the car sitting on the bump stops.
records.solution: Replace failed air struts with new OEM or aftermarket units from Arnott or Suncore. Replace the compressor if it no longer maintains pressure. For a permanent fix, some owners convert to conventional coilover suspension using kits from Strutmasters or BC Racing, which eliminates future air suspension issues.
symptoms: Vehicle sags on one corner overnight
Rough ride quality with bottoming out
Vehicle sits noticeably lower than normal

citations.title: ClubLexus.com — LS460 air suspension troubleshooting and conversion guide

communityRecommendations.content: Strutmasters LS460 coil spring conversion kit — eliminates the troublesome air suspension entirely with conventional springs and struts. Huge cost savings over repeatedly replacing air components.

records.title: Self-Leveling Headlight System Failure
records.description: The adaptive self-leveling HID headlight system fails due to deterioration of the headlight level sensors mounted at the front and rear suspension. The sensors develop internal failures from exposure to road debris and moisture, causing the headlights to aim incorrectly or trigger warning lights. Replacement sensors are expensive OEM-only parts.
records.solution: Replace the failed headlight leveling sensor(s). There are typically 3-4 sensors on the LS — two front and one or two rear. Use OEM sensors as aftermarket alternatives have poor fitment. Recalibrate the headlight system with a Lexus diagnostic scan tool after replacement.
symptoms: Headlight leveling warning message on dashboard
Headlights pointing too high or too low
Headlights not adjusting when vehicle is loaded

records.title: Noncompliant Aftermarket Corner/Bumper Lamp Assemblies
records.description: Some aftermarket combination corner and bumper lamp assemblies sold for 2001 applications were recalled because they failed to conform to federal lighting requirements. Poorly made lamp assemblies can reduce visibility, create fitment issues, and make the vehicle less conspicuous to other drivers.
records.solution: Inspect the vehicle for non-OEM or aftermarket front corner/bumper lamp assemblies, especially SaberSport units covered by the recall. Replace recalled or poor-quality lamps with OEM-equivalent assemblies, confirm bulb seating and aiming, and check for water intrusion or melted sockets. Costs vary depending on whether only the lamp housing or also bulbs and connectors need replacement.

records.title: Side/Curtain/Knee Airbag Inflator Defect
records.description: A documented safety issue exists on some 2004 Lexus LS vehicles involving improperly assembled air bag inflators used in the side air bag, curtain shield air bag, and knee air bag assemblies. The recall indicates inflators may have been produced with an assembly defect that could affect proper deployment performance in a crash.
records.solution: Verify recall completion for campaign 06V096000 through Lexus or NHTSA using the VIN. If incomplete, the remedy is replacement of the affected air bag inflator/module assemblies by a dealer at no charge; out-of-pocket repair outside recall can be expensive because it may involve side, curtain, or knee airbag modules and related trim removal. If the airbag warning light is on, scan the SRS system before replacing parts to confirm whether the recalled inflator or another component is at fault.

Potential improper air bag inflator assembly

records.title: Engine ECU/ECM electrolytic capacitor leakage (age-related)
records.description: The surface-mount electrolytic capacitors on the engine ECU (ECM) circuit board dry out, swell, and leak electrolyte over decades. The leaking acid corrodes the board traces and solder joints. This is one of the most widely documented age-related failures on the 1UZ-FE LS400 (and its SC400/Soarer siblings), and it worsens the older the car gets. Enthusiast consensus is that essentially every pre-1998 LS400/SC400 ECU is now degraded to some degree. Symptoms are erratic and intermittent, which makes it a notorious misdiagnosis trap where owners replace sensors, coils, and fuel components before finding the ECU is the root cause.
records.solution: Recap the ECU: desolder all the aged electrolytic capacitors, neutralize/clean any acid residue on the board, and install new low-ESR 105C-rated Japanese capacitors (Rubycon, Nichicon, Panasonic, Nippon Chemi-Con). 1990-92 boards use ~10-11 capacitors; 1993-94 use ~8. This is fine-pitch SMD work, not a first-time soldering job; many owners send the unit to a specialist recap/rebuild service instead.
symptoms: Random check-engine light / stored codes that don't match a bad part

records.title: Front lower ball joint wear and (rarely) separation
records.description: The front lower ball joints wear out with age and mileage and, in documented cases, have separated/sheared while driving — a serious safety concern at speed. Toyota's own maintenance schedule calls for ball-joint and suspension inspection at short intervals (about every 15,000 miles / 12 months), reflecting that these are wear items on the heavy LS400. Worn joints first show up as clunks and loose steering; total separation is the dangerous end state.
records.solution: Inspect the lower (and upper) ball joints for play at each service; replace worn joints in pairs. Use quality OEM/Aisin or reputable brands (Moog, 555) rather than the cheapest aftermarket, given the safety role. On many LS400s the ball joint is integral to the lower control arm, so a control-arm assembly may be required.
symptoms: Clunk or knock over bumps from the front
Wheel visibly loose at the joint in severe cases

records.title: Oil leaks from cam/crank seals, valve-cover gaskets, and timing cover
records.description: As the car ages, the elastomer seals and gaskets harden and weep oil. The most common sources are the valve-cover gaskets (oil drips onto the exhaust manifolds and produces a burning-oil smell), the front crankshaft and camshaft oil seals behind the timing cover, and the oil-pan gasket. On the 1998-2000 VVT-i engines, the O-ring inside the VVT-i cam phaser/gear is an additional documented leak point. Multiple sources typically leak at once on high-mileage cars.
records.solution: Replace the valve-cover gaskets (and spark-plug tube seals) for the top-end weep. For front-cover/crank/cam seal leaks, the timing belt and covers must come off — replace all three front oil seals together while access is open, ideally bundled with the timing-belt service to save labor.
symptoms: Oil drips/spots under the front of the engine
Smoke from engine bay off the exhaust manifolds

records.title: Starter motor failure buried under the intake manifold
records.description: The 1UZ-FE V8 mounts the starter in the engine valley, underneath the intake manifold, rather than at the side of the block. The starter solenoid contacts and motor wear out, typically between roughly 100,000 and 200,000 miles. The failure itself is ordinary, but the location makes it a labor-intensive job because the intake manifold must be removed to reach it. Two side complications are documented during the teardown: the plastic heater control valve commonly cracks and needs replacing, and the fragile variable-length intake runners can break if mishandled.
records.solution: Remove the intake manifold and replace the starter (a Denso reman/OEM unit is preferred for longevity). Owners are strongly advised to replace the heater control valve and any brittle vacuum/coolant hoses while the manifold is off, since access is otherwise costly to repeat. Use new intake and throttle-body gaskets on reassembly.

records.title: Timing belt / water pump service — interference risk on 1998-2000 VVT-i
records.description: The 1UZ-FE uses a rubber timing belt with a factory replacement interval of 90,000 miles or 7 years. A widely cited distinction: the 1990-1997 non-VVT-i engines are generally regarded as non-interference (a broken belt strands the car but typically does not smash valves), while the 1998-2000 VVT-i engines are commonly described as interference — a belt failure on those can cause valve-to-piston damage. On aging cars the belt itself is less often the failure point than a seized idler pulley or a failing water pump taking the belt out, so the whole kit must be serviced together.
records.solution: Replace the timing belt as a full kit at the interval: belt, both idler bearings, tensioner, and the water pump (driven by the belt). Inspect and replace the front crank and cam oil seals while the covers are off. Use OEM/Aisin or Gates components.
symptoms: Engine dies and won't restart if belt breaks
Coolant leak/overheating from failing water pump
Belt whine or rattle from a worn idler/tensioner
Coolant seepage at front of engine

records.title: Variable-assist power-steering pump/hose leaks (can kill the alternator)
records.description: The LS400 uses a variable-assist power-steering system (running ATF) whose pump seals and high-pressure hoses harden and leak with age. Because the power-steering pump sits directly above the alternator on the 1UZ-FE (worst on 1991-1997 cars), a leak drips fluid straight onto the alternator, contaminating it and causing premature charging failure. So a neglected PS leak commonly cascades into an alternator failure — the two are documented as a linked problem on these cars. Common leak points are the pump pulley/shaft seal and the high-pressure line.
records.solution: Replace the leaking power-steering pump seals and/or pressure hoses and clean up contamination promptly. If the alternator has been soaked/fouled, replace it (OEM/Denso reman). Address the leak first so a new alternator isn't ruined, and use the correct ATF (not conventional PS fluid).
symptoms: Charging warning light or dead battery from fouled alternator
Fluid dripping onto front of engine

records.title: Infotainment System Lag and Touchpad Frustration
records.description: The LS500 infotainment system suffers from significant input lag and an unintuitive touchpad controller that makes basic navigation tasks difficult while driving. The Remote Touch Interface trackpad requires excessive concentration to use accurately, and the system frequently freezes or responds slowly to inputs. This has been a consistent complaint since launch.
records.solution: Update to the latest infotainment software at the dealer, which improves responsiveness somewhat. Lexus has released multiple software updates since 2018. The 2022+ models received a touchscreen that partially addresses the issue. For older models, using voice commands or Apple CarPlay/Android Auto bypasses the native interface.
symptoms: Multi-second delay between input and screen response
Touchpad overshoots or misselects menu items
Navigation destination entry takes excessive time

citations.title: LexusEnthusiast.com — LS500 infotainment usability issues and software update history

communityRecommendations.content: Use voice commands for navigation and phone calls — it is significantly faster and safer than trying to use the touchpad while driving. Say "Hey Lexus" to activate.

records.title: 12.3-inch Infotainment / Lexus Interface Screen Freezing, Rebooting, or Going Blank
records.description: Owners of the current-generation LX have reported the center infotainment display freezing, rebooting, losing audio functions, or going black temporarily. Complaints and forum posts describe navigation, camera, and climate-related interface interruptions, sometimes resolved only by an ignition cycle or software update. The problem appears tied to head-unit software instability rather than a single hardware defect in many cases.
records.solution: Confirm software version and check for Lexus multimedia service bulletins or over-the-air/dealer updates. If the issue persists, dealers typically perform head-unit software reprogramming, inspect battery voltage and module communication faults, and replace the display/audio head unit only if updates do not resolve the problem. Owners should record when the failure occurs, especially if wireless phone projection is active.
symptoms: Backup or surround-view camera delayed or unavailable
Climate controls on screen become unresponsive

communityRecommendations.content: Owners commonly recommend updating the multimedia software first and temporarily disabling wireless Apple CarPlay/Android Auto if crashes are frequent.
If the screen goes blank intermittently, capture a video showing loss of camera or climate access to help the dealer justify module replacement.

records.title: AHC (Active Height Control) Suspension Failure
records.description: The Active Height Control hydraulic suspension on the LX570 develops leaks in the height control actuators, accumulator, and hydraulic lines. The system uses hydraulic fluid under high pressure to adjust ride height, and seals deteriorate over time causing fluid loss. A complete system failure leaves the vehicle stuck at one height setting and triggers warning lights.
records.solution: Replace failed AHC components — actuators, accumulator, or hydraulic lines as needed. A complete AHC overhaul runs $3,000-$6,000 at the dealer. Alternatively, convert to a conventional spring suspension using aftermarket kits that eliminate all hydraulic components.
symptoms: Vehicle sits lower than normal on one or more corners
Height control switch no longer adjusts ride height
Hydraulic fluid leak visible under vehicle

citations.title: ClubLexus.com — LX570 AHC suspension failure patterns and conversion options

communityRecommendations.content: Budget for AHC maintenance on any LX570 over 80,000 miles. The system is shared with the Toyota Land Cruiser 200, so LC forums have extensive repair documentation that applies directly.

records.title: Brake Pedal Vibration / Front Brake Rotor Warping and Premature Brake Pulsation
records.description: A number of current-generation LX owners have complained of steering wheel shake or brake pedal pulsation during moderate-to-hard braking, often at relatively low mileage for a full-size luxury SUV. Reports point to front rotor thickness variation or heat-related rotor distortion, especially on heavy vehicles used in urban driving or towing. While not unique to Lexus, the issue is documented enough in owner discussions and complaints to be considered a known pattern on this generation.
records.solution: Road-test the vehicle to confirm pulsation, then measure rotor runout and thickness variation. Dealers or independent shops typically resurface or replace front rotors and pads; if the problem recurs, verify caliper slide operation, wheel torque uniformity, and bedding-in procedure. Upgraded pad compounds or higher-quality replacement rotors are often suggested by owners who experienced repeat issues.
symptoms: Vibration at highway speeds when slowing down

communityRecommendations.content: Owners often recommend checking wheel lug torque after tire service because uneven torque can worsen rotor runout.
If replacing parts out of pocket, many suggest premium coated rotors and ceramic pads rather than simply resurfacing factory rotors.

records.title: Center Differential Lock Actuator Failure
records.description: The center differential lock actuator on the LX570 transfer case fails due to internal motor degradation and moisture intrusion. The actuator is responsible for engaging the center diff lock for off-road use, and when it fails, the lock cannot be engaged. This is the same basic design used on the Toyota Land Cruiser 200.
records.solution: Replace the center differential lock actuator motor assembly on the transfer case. The OEM Toyota part is recommended. After installation, perform a system initialization using a Toyota/Lexus diagnostic scanner. Test engagement on a loose surface in a straight line.
symptoms: Center diff lock will not engage when button is pressed
Center diff lock indicator light flashes and does not stay on
Clicking noise from transfer case area

citations.title: ClubLexus.com — LX570 center diff lock actuator replacement guide

communityRecommendations.content: Engage the center diff lock at least once a month to prevent the actuator from seizing due to inactivity. Even a 30-second engagement in a parking lot keeps the mechanism exercised.

records.title: Front Occupant Classification / Airbag Sensor Fault Triggering SRS Warning and Airbag Recall Repairs
records.description: Multiple 2022-2024 Lexus LX owners reported persistent SRS/airbag warning messages and dealer diagnoses related to the front passenger occupant classification system and related airbag components. This generation shares Toyota/Lexus safety-system campaigns affecting front seat occupant sensing and airbag readiness, and owners describe warning lights, repeated dealer visits, and concerns about whether the passenger airbag will deploy correctly. Because the issue directly affects restraint-system operation, it is considered high severity even when the repair itself is covered by recall or warranty.
records.solution: Scan the SRS system with a Toyota/Lexus-capable diagnostic tool and inspect the passenger seat weight/occupant classification components, seat harnesses, and any applicable recall campaign status by VIN. Dealers typically perform recall remedies, recalibration, or replacement of affected seat sensor/airbag-related parts, then clear codes and verify the occupant detection status with a seat calibration procedure. If the warning returns, wiring under the seat and connector tension should be checked carefully.
symptoms: Passenger airbag OFF/ON status behaving abnormally
Warning appears after moving front passenger seat
Repeated dealer visits for airbag-related faults

communityRecommendations.content: Before troubleshooting, check open recalls by VIN and avoid placing heavy items under the passenger seat that can stress connectors.
If the warning appears intermittently after seat movement, owners recommend documenting seat position changes and taking photos/video before dealer visits.

records.title: Power Tailgate / Rear Hatch Fails to Open or Close Properly Due to Latch or Strut/Module Faults
records.description: Owners have reported intermittent operation of the LX split rear hatch/power tailgate system, including failure to open, failure to cinch closed, or warning messages indicating the rear door is open when it appears latched. On a vehicle with a complex powered rear closure system, faults can stem from latch alignment, pinch sensors, control modules, or weak power strut behavior. The issue is inconvenient and can create security or battery-drain concerns if the vehicle thinks the hatch remains ajar.
records.solution: Inspect for stored body or back-door control codes, verify latch alignment, and test the power back-door motor/strut operation and anti-pinch sensors. Dealers may update control software, adjust the latch/striker, or replace the latch assembly or powered support components. If the hatch is intermittently reported open, check for water intrusion or connector issues in the rear door area.
symptoms: Tailgate starts to close then reverses
Rear door open warning stays on

communityRecommendations.content: Owners suggest cleaning and lightly lubricating the latch/striker area before assuming the power struts are bad.
If the hatch warning is intermittent, take photos of the cluster message and note whether it happens after rain or car washes.

records.title: V35A-FTS 3.4L Twin-Turbo V6 Main Bearing / Engine Failure Risk Covered by Toyota-Lexus Recall
records.description: The 2022+ Lexus LX uses the V35A-FTS twin-turbo V6 that is included in Toyota/Lexus campaigns for potential engine damage from machining debris and resulting main-bearing failure. Owners have reported knocking, reduced power, check-engine lights, and in some cases complete engine replacement. This is one of the most serious documented issues for the current LX because it can lead to sudden engine failure and very expensive repairs outside recall coverage.
records.solution: Check VIN for open engine recall/campaign status immediately. If symptoms such as knocking, low oil pressure warnings, or misfire/limp mode appear, the vehicle should not be driven until inspected; dealers may perform engine inspection and, where required by campaign procedure, short-block or complete engine replacement. Oil filter inspection for metallic debris and oil pressure verification are key diagnostic steps.

records.title: CVT Drone and Rubber Band Effect

The CVT holds the engine at high RPM while vehicle speed increases gradually, creating a disconnected feeling between throttle input and vehicle response that many owners find unpleasant.
records.solution: This is largely a design characteristic of the CVT, though software updates have improved the shift simulation logic. Visit the dealer for the latest ECU calibration. Using Sport mode provides more responsive behavior with simulated shift points that reduce the rubber band feeling.

records.title: Infotainment System Lag and Touchpad Issues

records.title: Battery Discharge and No-Start from DCM/Telematics Module Staying Awake
records.description: Multiple late-model Toyota/Lexus owners, including RC-platform owners, have reported intermittent dead 12V batteries after the vehicle sits for a short period. The pattern is consistent with the Data Communication Module (DCM)/telematics system not entering sleep mode, causing parasitic draw and eventual no-start conditions. Owners typically experience repeated jump-starts, battery replacement that does not permanently solve the issue, and dealer diagnosis pointing to abnormal key-off current draw.
records.solution: Confirm the complaint with a battery state-of-health test and a parasitic draw test after all modules should be asleep. If draw remains elevated, inspect DCM/telematics operation, software level, and related fuses/connectors; dealers typically apply software updates or replace the affected module if current draw remains out of spec. Battery replacement alone is often only a temporary fix unless the root parasitic draw is corrected.
symptoms: Dead battery after sitting overnight or a few days
Battery tests good initially but goes dead again
Intermittent warning messages after low-voltage event

communityRecommendations.content: Have the dealer measure key-off parasitic draw after full sleep timeout; ask specifically whether the DCM/telematics module has applicable software updates or replacement guidance.
If the car is driven infrequently, owners often use a smart battery maintainer until the root cause is fixed.

records.title: Brake Pedal Vibration or Pulsation from Front Rotor Thickness Variation
records.description: Owners of current RC models continue to report steering wheel shake or brake pedal pulsation during moderate-to-hard braking, often at relatively low mileage. In many cases the underlying issue is rotor thickness variation or pad material transfer rather than a true one-time rotor 'warp.' The symptom is more noticeable after repeated heat cycles, aggressive driving, or long periods of light use followed by harder braking.
records.solution: Road-test to confirm pulsation and measure rotor runout and thickness variation with a dial indicator/micrometer. If out of spec, resurface or replace rotors and pads as a set, clean hub mating surfaces, and properly torque wheels to prevent recurrence. A proper bed-in procedure for new pads/rotors helps reduce repeat complaints.

records.title: Infotainment Screen Freezing, CarPlay/Android Auto Disconnects, and Audio Rebooting
records.description: Owners have reported intermittent multimedia glitches on newer Lexus vehicles using the current infotainment stack, including frozen screens, delayed boot-up, dropped CarPlay/Android Auto sessions, and occasional audio loss until the system is restarted. records.title: Interior Rattle and Buzzing from Door Panels, Dash, and Rear Trim at Highway Speeds
records.description: A recurring owner complaint on the RC coupe is trim-related rattles, especially from the door panels, dashboard area, and rear interior trim/shelf. The coupe body style, low-profile tires, and firm suspension tuning can transmit enough vibration to create intermittent buzzes that are difficult to duplicate at the dealer. While not a mechanical failure, the issue is well documented by owners and can be persistent on rough pavement or in cold weather.
records.solution: Technicians usually need a ride-along to isolate the exact source, then remove trim panels and apply felt tape, foam isolators, or revised clips where panels contact each other. Re-torquing loose fasteners and checking for items in the trunk/rear shelf area can eliminate many noises. Because the problem is often intermittent, documenting road speed, temperature, and road surface helps diagnosis.
symptoms: Rear shelf or rear trim noise
Rattle more noticeable in cold weather

records.title: 12V Battery Discharge and No-Start from Telematics/DCM Staying Awake
records.description: Multiple 2023-2025 RX owners have reported dead 12V batteries, repeated jump-starts, and intermittent no-start conditions after the vehicle sits overnight or for a few days. The issue has been tied in owner reports and Toyota/Lexus service communications to excessive parasitic draw, often involving the Data Communication Module (DCM)/telematics system or related control modules not entering sleep mode properly. Owners commonly describe the problem appearing on relatively new vehicles with otherwise healthy batteries.
records.solution: Diagnosis should start with a battery state-of-health test and a parasitic draw test after all modules are expected to sleep. Dealers typically check for applicable software updates or service bulletins addressing DCM/module sleep behavior, then recharge or replace the battery if it has been damaged by repeated deep discharge. If draw remains high, isolate the offending circuit and verify telematics, gateway, and body ECU software calibration levels.
symptoms: warning messages after low voltage event
battery replacement does not permanently solve issue

communityRecommendations.content: Ask the dealer to document parasitic draw in milliamps after sleep timeout and verify all telematics/DCM software updates are installed before authorizing another battery replacement.
If the vehicle must sit for long periods, owners often use a smart maintainer to prevent deep discharge while the root cause is being diagnosed.

records.title: AC Evaporator Core Refrigerant Leak
records.description: The AC evaporator core in the RX develops pinhole leaks from internal corrosion, causing slow refrigerant loss. The system gradually loses cooling capacity over weeks or months as the charge leaks through the evaporator. This is an expensive repair because the entire dashboard must be removed to access the evaporator.
records.solution: Replace the AC evaporator core and receiver/drier. This requires full dashboard removal, which is 8-12 hours of labor. Recharge the system with the correct amount of R-134a refrigerant. Replacing the expansion valve at the same time is recommended while the dash is apart.
symptoms: AC gradually stops blowing cold air

Humidity or fog on windshield when using AC
Visible refrigerant dye leak at evaporator drain

communityRecommendations.content: Before paying for evaporator replacement, have a UV dye test done to confirm the evaporator is the source. The condenser and compressor seals are much cheaper to replace and should be ruled out first.

records.title: Brake Pedal Vibration/Grinding and Extended Stopping Feel from ABS Actuator Software Logic
records.description: Some current-generation RX owners report an unexpectedly harsh ABS event at low speeds over bumps, manhole covers, or rough pavement, accompanied by grinding or pedal kickback and a sensation of reduced braking for a moment. This complaint pattern has appeared on Toyota/Lexus TNGA-K vehicles and is documented in owner discussions and complaints, where drivers describe the vehicle seeming to surge forward briefly while the ABS modulates. While often intermittent, it can be alarming in urban stop-and-go driving.
records.solution: Road-test the vehicle on the same surface conditions to reproduce the concern and scan the brake/ABS system for stored codes. Dealers should check for calibration updates to the skid control ECU/ABS software and inspect wheel-speed sensor tone rings, tire size uniformity, and suspension components that could trigger false wheel-slip detection. If no hardware fault is found, software reprogramming is the most common corrective path.

communityRecommendations.content: When visiting the dealer, note the exact speed, road surface, and whether the steering wheel was turned; reproducible conditions help separate normal ABS behavior from a calibration issue.
Verify all four tires match in size, wear, and pressure, since wheel-speed differences can aggravate false ABS intervention.

records.title: Dashboard Melting and Sticky Surface
records.description: The RX350 and RX450h dashboards develop the same melting, sticky surface defect seen across the Lexus lineup. The dashboard material chemically degrades in heat and sunlight, creating a reflective glare hazard on the windshield. The RX is the highest-volume model affected, generating the most complaints to NHTSA.
records.solution: Dashboard replacement under Lexus Customer Support Program ZE7. The RX was one of the first models covered due to the high volume of complaints. Contact your Lexus dealer or call 1-800-255-3987 for eligibility verification.
symptoms: Dashboard surface becomes sticky and shiny

citations.title: NHTSA complaint cluster — Lexus RX dashboard melting (3,500+ complaints, highest among Lexus models)

communityRecommendations.content: The RX has the best coverage track record for goodwill dashboard replacements. Even 2007-2009 models have received free replacements years after the warranty extension officially ended.

records.title: Front Camera / Millimeter-Wave Radar Misalignment Causing PCS and Driver-Assist Warnings
records.description: Owners of the current-generation RX have reported recurring messages such as 'Pre-Collision System Malfunction,' 'Front Camera Unavailable,' or temporary loss of adaptive cruise and lane functions. These complaints appear in NHTSA filings and owner forums, often after windshield replacement, minor impacts, heavy rain, or sometimes with no obvious trigger. The issue is commonly related to camera/radar obstruction, calibration drift, connector faults, or software sensitivity in the Lexus Safety System+ suite.
records.solution: Inspect the windshield camera area and front radar emblem area for dirt, condensation, damage, or non-OEM replacement parts. Perform a scan for ADAS-related DTCs, then complete static/dynamic calibration of the forward recognition camera and millimeter-wave radar if alignment is out of spec. If warnings persist, dealers may apply software updates or replace a faulty sensor/module after confirming power, ground, and network integrity.

communityRecommendations.content: After any windshield replacement, confirm the shop can perform Lexus-compatible ADAS calibration; many intermittent warnings start after glass work.
Keep the radar emblem and upper windshield camera area clean and avoid stickers, dashcams, or tint strips that can interfere with the sensors.

records.title: Infotainment Screen Freezing, Wireless CarPlay/Android Auto Dropouts, and Rebooting Head Unit
records.description: The new-generation RX uses Lexus Interface, and owners have widely reported frozen center displays, laggy touch response, black screens, audio loss, and unstable wireless smartphone integration. Complaints and forum threads describe random head-unit reboots, failure to reconnect to Apple CarPlay or Android Auto, and navigation/audio functions becoming unavailable until the vehicle is restarted. The pattern suggests a mix of software bugs, phone compatibility issues, and occasional hardware faults.
records.solution: First verify the head unit has the latest Lexus Interface software and update the connected phone OS. Delete and re-pair the phone, test both wireless and wired connections, and check for TSBs or dealer software campaigns addressing multimedia instability. If the unit continues freezing or rebooting, dealers may replace the display/audio ECU or related USB hub after documenting the failure.

communityRecommendations.content: Owners often report better stability after removing old phone pairings, rebooting the phone, and re-pairing only one primary device.
If wireless CarPlay remains unreliable, use a high-quality USB-C cable temporarily to determine whether the issue is wireless-stack related.

records.title: Excessive Oil Consumption 2GR Engine
records.description: The 3.5L 2GR-FE V6 in the RX350 consumes excessive oil, often requiring a quart every 1,500-3,000 miles. The piston ring design allows oil to bypass into the combustion chamber, and the PCV system contributes to the problem. Toyota acknowledged the issue with a TSB covering piston ring replacement.
records.solution: Dealer oil consumption test to document the rate. If excessive, piston ring replacement is the definitive fix under Toyota TSB. Check and clean the PCV valve as a first step. Monitor oil level weekly and keep a log of consumption for warranty claims.
symptoms: Oil level drops 1+ quart between changes
Fouled spark plugs from oil burning

citations.title: Toyota TSB 0094-14 — 2GR-FE oil consumption diagnosis and piston ring replacement

communityRecommendations.content: Switching from 0W-20 to 5W-30 synthetic (Toyota also approves this weight) has reduced oil consumption by 30-50% for many RX350 owners without voiding warranty.

records.title: Power Steering Pressure Hose Leak and Pump Whine from Fluid Loss
records.description: Both RX300 and RX330 generations commonly develop power steering fluid leaks, especially from the high-pressure hose and related line connections. Owners report red fluid on the driveway, groaning or whining while turning, and heavier steering effort as fluid level drops. If ignored, the pump can run dry and fail, increasing repair cost significantly.
records.solution: Inspect the pressure hose, return lines, reservoir, and pump area for wetness, then confirm whether the leak is from the crimped hose section or a fitting. Replace the leaking hose or line assembly, refill with the correct fluid, and bleed the system fully; if the pump has been noisy for long, inspect for internal damage. Cleaning the subframe and alternator area is important because leaked fluid can spread widely.
symptoms: Fluid on driveway or under engine cradle

communityRecommendations.content: Owners recommend replacing aging return hoses at the same time as the pressure hose if they are soft or sweating, since labor overlap is significant.
After repair, bleed the steering system with the front wheels raised to reduce pump cavitation noise.

records.title: Rear Main Seal / Engine Oil Leak at Timing Cover and Lower Engine Seals
records.description: RX330 owners frequently report persistent engine oil leaks that are often diagnosed at the rear main seal, timing cover area, or other lower engine sealing surfaces. The leak may start as minor seepage but can progress to oil spots on the driveway, burning oil odor, and contamination of the lower engine and subframe. Because access is labor-intensive, especially if the rear main seal is involved, repair costs can become substantial even when the leak itself is not immediately catastrophic.
records.solution: Clean the engine thoroughly and use dye or UV tracing to identify the true source, since valve cover, timing cover, and rear main leaks can be misidentified. Repair involves replacing the failed seal or resealing the timing cover, often while addressing nearby components with overlapping labor. If the leak is minor, some owners monitor oil level until the leak worsens enough to justify the labor.
symptoms: Oil residue on lower engine or transmission bellhousing
Smoke from oil contacting hot exhaust components

communityRecommendations.content: Use UV dye before authorizing a rear main seal job; several owners found the actual leak was higher up at the valve cover or timing cover.
If transmission removal is required, owners often replace related wear items with overlapping labor to save money later.

records.title: Steering Intermediate Shaft Clunk and Loose Steering Feel Over Bumps
records.description: Second-generation RX330 models commonly develop a clunk or knock felt through the steering column, especially at low speed over small bumps or during quick steering inputs. Lexus issued service information for intermediate steering shaft noise, and owners often describe the sensation as a loose front end despite no obvious play in major suspension joints. The condition is usually caused by wear or lash in the intermediate shaft splines or joints rather than a catastrophic steering rack failure.
records.solution: Road test over small road imperfections to reproduce the column knock, then isolate the sound from the shaft, rack mounts, and front suspension links. Replacement of the intermediate steering shaft is the usual fix; some vehicles also need inspection of rack bushings and front stabilizer links if multiple noises are present. An alignment is not always required but front-end inspection should accompany the repair.
symptoms: Noise during quick left-right steering input
Front-end rattle with no obvious suspension failure

communityRecommendations.content: Owners recommend confirming the noise source before replacing struts or sway bar links, because the steering shaft clunk can mimic suspension noise.
Use the updated Lexus/Toyota shaft part rather than a salvage-yard original to reduce the chance of repeat noise.

records.title: 8-Speed Automatic Transmission Shudder
records.description: The Aisin 8-speed automatic in the fourth-generation RX develops a noticeable shudder or vibration during light throttle acceleration, particularly in the 25-45 MPH range during torque converter lockup. The shudder is caused by torque converter clutch material wearing into the transmission fluid, degrading its friction properties.
records.solution: Perform a transmission fluid drain-and-fill with Toyota WS ATF, which resolves the shudder in most cases. Severe cases may require a torque converter replacement. Do not flush — only drain and refill. Plan to change the fluid every 30,000-40,000 miles despite the "lifetime" fluid claim.
symptoms: Feeling like driving over rumble strips
Vibration disappears under heavy throttle or braking

citations.title: Lexus TSB L-SB-0162-19 — RX350 transmission shudder fluid change procedure

communityRecommendations.content: A simple drain-and-fill of Toyota WS ATF fixes the shudder in 90% of cases. Do 2-3 drain-and-fill cycles over 10,000 miles to fully flush the old contaminated fluid.

records.title: U140E/U151E Automatic Transmission Failure from Burned Planetary Gearset and Delayed Engagement
records.description: Early first-generation RX300 models are well known for premature automatic transmission failure, especially on AWD vehicles but also on FWD examples. Owners report delayed engagement into Drive or Reverse, harsh shifting, slipping on acceleration, and eventual loss of movement; teardown reports commonly cite burned clutches and damaged planetary gear components. The issue is widely documented in owner communities, repair databases, and NHTSA complaints, and is often attributed to a transmission that runs hot and is heavily stressed by vehicle weight.
records.solution: Diagnosis usually starts with checking fluid condition, line pressure behavior, and whether engagement delay or flare shifts are present when warm. In most cases, fluid changes do not cure an already failing unit; the durable fix is a quality rebuild or replacement transmission, often with updated hard parts and careful inspection of the cooler and valve body. Many owners also add an auxiliary transmission cooler after replacement to reduce repeat failures.
symptoms: Delayed engagement into Drive or Reverse
Engine revs increase with little vehicle movement

citations.title: CarComplaints: Lexus RX300 Transmission Problems

communityRecommendations.content: If replacing the transmission, owners commonly recommend installing an external transmission cooler and fully flushing cooler lines to avoid contaminating the rebuilt unit.
Use Toyota Type T-IV compatible fluid and avoid generic fluid mixes on these early Aisin units.

records.title: Water Pump Premature Failure
records.description: The water pump on the RX fails prematurely due to internal seal and bearing wear. Coolant weeps from the pump weep hole and the bearing develops play, causing a whining or grinding noise from the front of the engine. Failure rates are highest between 60,000-100,000 miles.
records.solution: Replace the water pump and thermostat assembly. Use OEM Aisin or Denso parts for reliability. Replace the drive belt and tensioner at the same time. Flush the cooling system with new Toyota Super Long Life Coolant during the repair.
symptoms: Coolant leak from water pump area
Whining noise from front of engine

citations.title: ClubLexus.com — RX350 water pump replacement interval and recommended parts

communityRecommendations.content: Aisin WPT-190 water pump — OEM supplier quality at aftermarket pricing. Comes with gasket and o-ring. Pair with an Aisin thermostat for a complete cooling system refresh.

claims.content: Aisin WPT-190 water pump — OEM supplier quality at aftermarket pricing. Comes with gasket and o-ring. Pair with an Aisin thermostat for a complete cooling system refresh.

records.title: AC Compressor Clutch and Bearing Failure
records.description: The AC compressor on the SC430 suffers from clutch and bearing failure, particularly on vehicles in hot climates where the AC system runs constantly. The compressor clutch plate wears and the bearing develops excessive play, eventually causing the compressor to seize. When the compressor fails, it sends metal debris through the AC system.
records.solution: Replace the AC compressor, receiver/drier, and expansion valve. Flush the entire AC system to remove any metal debris from the failed compressor. Recharge with R-134a refrigerant. If debris is found, the condenser should also be replaced to prevent contaminating the new compressor.
symptoms: AC compressor makes clicking or grinding noise
Squealing noise from AC belt area
AC clutch engages and disengages rapidly

citations.title: ClubLexus.com — SC430 AC compressor replacement guide and system flush procedure

communityRecommendations.content: Always replace the receiver/drier and flush the system when replacing the compressor. Metal debris from a failed compressor will destroy the new one within months if not fully cleaned out.

records.title: Dashboard Melting and Sticky Surface
records.description: The SC430 dashboard develops the same sticky, melting surface as other Lexus models from this era. The convertible design exposes the dashboard to even more direct sunlight than sedan models, accelerating the deterioration. The dashboard material becomes dangerously reflective on the windshield.
records.solution: Dashboard replacement under Lexus Customer Support Program ZE7. The SC430 is covered under the same program as the ES, IS, and RX. Contact Lexus corporate if the dealer is unresponsive.
symptoms: Reflective glare on windshield especially with top down

citations.title: NHTSA complaints — Lexus SC430 dashboard melting, exacerbated by convertible sun exposure

communityRecommendations.content: SC430 owners with the convertible top should always use a windshield sun shade when parked — the direct sun exposure through the retractable hardtop area accelerates dashboard melting significantly.

records.title: Timing Belt Service Critical Interval
records.description: The SC430 uses the 3UZ-FE V8 with a timing belt that must be replaced at 90,000-mile intervals. The 3UZ-FE is an interference engine, meaning a broken timing belt causes pistons to strike valves, resulting in catastrophic engine damage. Many SC430 owners are unaware of this critical service interval because the car is often a low-mileage garage queen.
records.solution: Replace the timing belt, tensioner, idler pulleys, and water pump as a complete kit every 90,000 miles or 9 years, whichever comes first. Age-based replacement is particularly important for SC430s that accumulate low annual mileage, as the belt rubber degrades with age regardless of mileage.
symptoms: Ticking noise from front of engine
Engine stops suddenly while driving (belt failure)
Coolant leak from water pump weep hole

citations.title: ClubLexus.com — SC430 timing belt replacement guide with complete part numbers and torque specs

communityRecommendations.content: Gates TCKWP271 timing belt kit with water pump — complete kit for the 3UZ-FE including belt, hydraulic tensioner, idler pulleys, and Aisin water pump.

records.title: A340E Automatic Transmission Wear (Overdrive Slip / Torque-Converter Shudder)
records.description: The 4-speed A340E automatic in the SC300 is durable but, on neglected examples, begins showing age around 130,000-150,000 miles: slipping out of overdrive, delayed engagement, and a shudder at highway speed from a worn torque-converter lockup clutch. The valve body and shift solenoids degrade from heat cycling, and most used SC300s have never had a proper fluid/filter service, which accelerates the wear. No recalls are tied to this; it is age/maintenance related.
records.solution: Perform a proper fluid and filter service using Toyota Type T-IV ATF as preventive care. If shudder/slip is already present, address the torque converter, valve body, and shift solenoids; a full A340E rebuild (roughly $1,800-$2,500) is the fix for advanced wear.
symptoms: Harsh or delayed shifting when cold

citations.title: Wont Shift into Overdrive - ClubLexus

records.title: Distributor Cap & Rotor Cracking / Ignition Misfire (Non-VVT-i 1992-1997)
records.description: Pre-VVT-i 2JZ-GE SC300s (1992-1997) use a cam-driven distributor. With age the cap and rotor crack; spark then jumps through the crack, burning a hole in the rotor and causing misfires, rough cold idle, and shaking at idle. A leaking valve-cover gasket that lets oil pool in the spark-plug tubes produces overlapping misfire symptoms, so both should be inspected together. (The 1998-2000 VVT-i engine is distributorless with individual coils, so this applies only to the non-VVT-i years.)
records.solution: Replace the distributor cap and rotor (or a good remanufactured distributor if the shaft/bearing is worn); replace the valve cover gasket and spark-plug tube seals if oil is present in the plug wells, and inspect/clean the throttle body. Replace brittle plug wires as preventive maintenance.
symptoms: Oil in spark-plug tubes (related valve-cover leak)

citations.title: Ignition Distributor Cap And Rotor - Lexus Owners Club

records.title: Front Lower Control Arm Bushing & Ball Joint Wear (Clunk Over Bumps)
records.description: The front lower control arm rubber bushings wear out with age, allowing slop that produces a clunk or knock over bumps and during rapid speed changes, plus vague steering. On the SC, the lower ball joint is integral to the control arm and is not separately serviceable, so a worn ball joint requires the whole arm. Supra MkIV (JZA80) lower control arms interchange and are often cheaper than Lexus units; polyurethane bushing kits are also available.
records.solution: Replace worn bushings (OEM rubber or polyurethane) to eliminate the clunk; if the integral ball joint is also worn, replace the complete lower control arm assembly (later-gen Supra arms interchange; note JZA70 arms do NOT fit). Do both sides and align afterward.

citations.title: Confirmed (With Pics): Supra Lower Control Arms on Lexus SC-300 - ClubLexus
