records.title: Power Steering Pump Seal Leak Contaminating the Alternator
records.description: The power steering pump on the first-gen SC develops a faulty seal that leaks power steering fluid. Because the alternator sits directly below the pump, the fluid can drip onto it. If neglected, the fluid saturates and destroys the alternator, turning a modest seal leak into a two-part failure. This is a widely cited SC300/SC400 (and shared LS400) age-related issue; the pump seals and pressure valve commonly fail from heat past ~100k miles.
records.solution: Reseal or replace the power steering pump before fluid reaches the alternator; clean/inspect the alternator, and replace it if already fluid-soaked. Address the pressure control valve if it is the leak source. Doing both the pump and alternator together is common practice when the alternator is contaminated.
symptoms: Power steering fluid leak / low reservoir

citations.title: SC400 power steering pump leak - ClubLexus
Lexus SC400 Problems - ThreePiece.us

records.title: Power Window Regulator Nylon Carrier Failure
records.description: The SC300/SC400 door window regulators use a plastic/nylon carrier that holds a steel block on the lift cable. With age the nylon cracks and the ears break, allowing the steel block to tear through the guide. The glass then goes crooked, drops into the door, or the motor spins without moving the window. A clicking or POP sound during window travel is the classic early warning. Aggravated by dried outer window sweep rubber that drags on the glass.
records.solution: Replace the window regulator (OEM or quality aftermarket); replace the dried/worn outer window sweeps to reduce drag. Temporary adhesive/J-B Weld repairs of the carrier are known to fail after only a handful of cycles; durable DIY fixes reinforce the nylon carrier with drilled holes and metal.
symptoms: Clicking or pop sound when window moves
Window sits crooked in the track
Glass drops into door and won't return
Motor runs but window doesn't move

citations.title: SC300 SC400 Window Regulator Fix - New Technique - ClubLexus
Window Regulator Replacement - Lexus Owners Club

records.title: VVT-i Cam Gear O-Ring / Intake Cam Seal Oil Leak (1998-2000 VVT-i 2JZ-GE)
records.description: On the VVT-i version of the 2JZ-GE (introduced on the SC300 for the 1998 model year and produced through the end of the run in 2000), the intake cam VVT-i gear/actuator uses an internal O-ring that hardens with age and heat, allowing oil to weep from the front of the cylinder head near the timing cover. It is one of the most commonly reported oil leaks on high-mileage VVT-i 2JZ-GE engines (shared with the GS300/IS300 siblings). Toyota advises against disassembling the VVT-i gear (gear backlash risk), so many owners address it by replacing the O-ring with an aftermarket Viton/FKM kit or replacing the front cam seal.
records.solution: Replace the VVT-i cam gear O-ring (aftermarket Viton/FKM rebuild kit) and/or the front intake camshaft oil seal. Inspect the timing-belt-area seals at the same time and replace the timing belt if due since access overlaps. Use OEM or high-temp Viton seals to prevent recurrence. Dealers typically only sell the complete VVT-i gear (~$350) rather than the O-ring alone.
symptoms: Oil weeping/dripping from front of engine near timing cover
Oil residue on lower front of block

citations.title: VVTi cam gear leaking oil - Lexus IS Forum (my.is)
VVTi cam gear/cam seal oil leak - ClubLexus

records.title: Climate Control LCD Pixel Fade and Dim Backlighting
records.description: The factory climate control head unit suffers from two well-documented age-related failures: the LCD display loses pixels (rows of segments go black, making temperature and fan speed unreadable) and the incandescent backlight bulbs burn out, leaving the unit dim or completely dark at night. The conductive rubber zebra strip between the PCB and LCD degrades over time, and the small bulbs behind the faceplate are not designed for the heat cycles they see.
records.solution: Remove the climate control unit (held in by trim clips and two screws) and either send it to a specialist like Tanin Auto Electronix for LCD/bulb refurbishment, or DIY the repair using a replacement LCD screen and LED bulb kit. The fix typically restores full functionality with a lifetime warranty from reputable rebuilders. Avoid generic 12V replacement bulbs as they produce uneven brightness compared to the rest of the dash.
symptoms: Missing or fading pixels on the climate control LCD
Dim or completely dark backlight on the HVAC display
Unable to read temperature setting or fan speed at night
Display ghosting or partial segments visible

records.title: CVT Hesitation and Sluggish Response
records.description: The UX200 Direct Shift CVT and UX250h eCVT both exhibit noticeable hesitation when accelerating from a stop and during passing maneuvers. The transmission response is delayed by 1-2 seconds after pressing the accelerator, which is particularly noticeable when merging into traffic or making left turns across oncoming traffic.
records.solution: Update to the latest transmission ECU calibration at the dealer, which improves tip-in response. Use Sport mode for situations requiring quicker response. The UX250h hybrid has better low-speed response than the UX200 due to the electric motor providing instant torque.
symptoms: Sluggish response when merging onto highway
Engine revs but vehicle does not accelerate proportionally

citations.title: ClubLexus.com — UX200/UX250h CVT response and hesitation complaints thread

communityRecommendations.content: Left-foot braking lightly while pressing the accelerator eliminates the hesitation by pre-loading the drivetrain. This is a common technique for Toyota/Lexus CVT-equipped vehicles.

records.title: Infotainment System Lag and Touchpad Frustration
records.description: The UX shares the same frustrating Remote Touch Interface touchpad and laggy infotainment system as other Lexus models. The small screen and imprecise touchpad make basic operations like changing radio stations or entering navigation destinations unnecessarily difficult. The system is slow to boot and respond to inputs.
records.solution: Update infotainment software to the latest version. The 2020+ models can have Apple CarPlay/Android Auto added, which dramatically improves the user experience. Use voice commands for navigation and phone functions to avoid the touchpad entirely.
symptoms: Slow screen response to touchpad inputs

citations.title: LexusOwnersClub.com — UX infotainment complaints and Apple CarPlay retrofit discussion

communityRecommendations.content: If your UX does not have Apple CarPlay, ask your dealer about the retrofit — Lexus offers a dealer-installed upgrade for 2019-2020 models that adds CarPlay support and dramatically improves daily usability.
